summary: Xiaomi LLM Core authors (with interns from PKU, HKU and RUC) present an agentic pipeline that builds RL tasks from existing open-source repos. Agents remove implemented functionality, write a behaviour-only task statement, build hidden tests by executing the original code, and filter tasks with six-container fail-to-pass checks, adversarial leakage rollouts, an agent reviewer of verifier verdicts, and a mixed pass/fail screen under a frontier model. The result is 5,545 tasks from 3,185 repos in 23 languages. GRPO training of Xiaomi's own MiMo-V2.5 raises DeepSWE from 10.0 to 21.7, ProgramBench Almost-Solved from 4.5 to 21.5, and Terminal-Bench v2.1 from 63.7 to 72.2, and filtered 3k/5k pools beat an unfiltered 8k pool.

claims.claim: RL on CodeMidas improves the agent on all five external benchmarks
claims.evidence: Fig. 5 / §4.2: DeepSWE 10.0->21.7, ProgramBench 4.5->21.5, Terminal-Bench v2.1 63.7->72.2. SWE-bench Pro and RepoZero C2Rust appear only in the figure. One trained model, one training run, no variance, compared only with the untrained initial policy. The abstract's '+11.7%' figures are percentage points.

claims.claim: Cleaning and filtering matter more than raw task count
claims.evidence: §5.1, Fig. 8: filtered 5k beats unfiltered 8k by 0.59 / 4.59 / 4.49 pp on SWE-bench Pro / DeepSWE / CodeMidas Val, and 3k also beats 8k. Single run per pool. All filters are removed together, so no individual filter is isolated. The SWE-bench Pro margin is small.
1k/3k/5k: DeepSWE 17.57/19.05/21.70; Val 41.30/43.22/44.73. Three points, single runs, no CIs.

claims.claim: RL makes agents explore codebases more and self-verify more diversely, and these behaviours generalize
claims.evidence: Table 2: pre-edit read/search calls 27.2->40.1; distinct verification commands 2.03->2.53. Table 3 shows similar shifts on held-out benchmarks. Self-verification is associated with +4.2 pp pass (CI 1.8-6.6), but exploration is not (+0.7 pp, CI -1.9 to 3.7). Correlational.

claims.claim: Source code alone is a better or more scalable basis for RL environments than issue- or commit-derived pipelines
claims.evidence: Only a qualitative input-requirements table (Table 1). No training comparison against SWE-smith, R2E-Gym, SWE-rebench V2 or SWE-Universe data at equal compute.

patterns.note: Gains are measured against the untrained initial policy only, with no competing dataset at equal compute, a single run, and a single model. The only isolating comparison is filtered vs unfiltered CodeMidas data.
Hidden execution-grounded tests with fail-to-pass checks across six containers as the binary reward, plus agent review of false positives and negatives. The individual filters are not ablated.
Pre-edit exploration calls rise after RL (27->40), but exploration is not associated with higher pass rate (+0.7 pp, CI crosses zero).
Each generated test records the requirement it covers. The links are not verified or reported.
A reviewing agent judges whether rollouts satisfy the statement in order to flag verifier defects. Its accuracy is not reported.

methodology.sample: 5,545 training tasks from 3,185 repos, 23 languages (Python 21.4%, TypeScript 18.3%, Go 16.2%, C++ 12.5%, JavaScript 11.3%; Java share not reported). Eval on SWE-bench Pro, DeepSWE v1.1, ProgramBench, RepoZero C2Rust and Terminal-Bench v2.1, plus a 200-task CodeMidas Val (3 attempts).
methodology.baselines: Initial MiMo-V2.5 policy and an unfiltered 8k CodeMidas sample. No other RL environment dataset.
methodology.models: MiMo-V2.5 only (trained with GRPO). Construction, reviewer and screening agents and the 'frontier model' are not named.
methodology.variance: None for benchmark gains; single training run per pool. Bootstrap CIs only for behaviour-success associations.
methodology.ablations: Task-pool scale (1k/3k/5k); all filtering vs none (8k)
methodology.contamination_controls: Training tasks stated disjoint from CodeMidas Val and the five benchmark task sets; no check against pretraining exposure of source repos

standards.artifacts: No dataset, code or environment release stated; training hyperparameters in Appendix A

biases.detail: Gains are relative to the untrained initial policy, not to training on existing environment datasets.
Only Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.5 is trained and evaluated.
Single runs, no seeds or CIs on benchmark scores; several deltas are under 1 pp.
The vendor's pipeline trains the vendor's model and is scored on a vendor-built validation set alongside public benchmarks.
No release of the 5,545 tasks, the pipeline, or the agents' prompts.
Construction spends agentic compute on every stage (multiple agents, six containers, four solution rollouts, adversarial rollouts), but it is not quantified.
Percentage-point gains are written as '%'; 'Midas touch' framing.

coi.affiliations: LLM Core, Xiaomi (most authors and co-corresponding author); Peking University; University of Hong Kong; Renmin University of China
coi.funding: not stated (work done during Xiaomi internships)
coi.detail: A vendor improves its own model with its own unreleased data and reports only gains over its own starting point. It makes no ranking claim against competitors, which limits the promotional risk.

verdict_reason: In scope (coding-agent training) but nearly irrelevant to the discovery harness. The evidence is one model, one run, compared with the untrained policy, with no artifacts. The filtered-vs-unfiltered comparison is the only isolating result.
applicability: The team does not RL-train models, so the headline does not transfer. The construction recipe can be reused to build internal onboarding exercises or agent evals from the team's own Java ingestion repos. Delete an implemented feature, write a behaviour-only statement, generate tests by running the original code, strip assertions on wording or private symbols, and run an adversarial 'find the leaked answer' pass. The convention of recording which requirement each test covers is a cheap step toward requirement-to-test traceability, though it is unverified here. More exploration after RL was not linked to success, so this says nothing about whether exploration subagents help.
